Invoke at least one permitted information retrieval tool querying approved synthetic business records
Extract and validate relevant document snippets while filtering out irrelevant noise
Formulate clear, conversational, and factually grounded responses strictly supported by retrieved facts
Provide explicit source attribution and document references for every factual claim made
Detect missing or ambiguous information and gracefully inform the user rather than guessing
Log observable tool invocations, parameters, and latency in an audit trace
Enforce strict read-only permissions preventing unauthorized data manipulation

Approved synthetic knowledge repository (FAQ catalog, course specs, or product data)
JSON-based tool schema defining the search/lookup function parameters and return contracts
Verified tool invocation trace showing query parameters, returned snippets, and execution latency
Grounded response demonstrations including transparent source citations (e.g., '[Doc: Course-Catalog-2027, Sec: 4.2]')

If a human manager rejects the action, the agent must abort execution safely and notify the requester.

Validate mandatory parameter fields and reject malformed or incomplete submissions

Generate a structured approval payload presenting proposed action, entity ID, and reason to the human reviewer

Gracefully handle rejection events, informing the requester of the reviewer's decision without modifying state
Maintain an immutable execution trace recording inputs, decisions, approvals, and outcomes

Allowed action inventory and tool permission matrix (distinguishing read-only vs sensitive write operations)
JSON tool schemas with parameter validation contracts for all connected tools
Interactive human approval flow demonstration (via mock Slack alert or web approval prompt)
Rejection branch demonstration showing clean abort behavior when human manager denies the action

faq.question: What is the AI Agents Fundamentals course?
faq.answer: AI Agents Fundamentals: Design, Tools & Safety is a foundational, practical certification course that teaches you how to design, prototype, and evaluate tool-using AI agents. Unlike ordinary chatbots that only generate conversational text, agents decompose tasks, select and execute permitted tools, access document-grounded knowledge, and perform multi-step workflows under strict human oversight and safety guardrails.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The course is structured for beginners and intermediate learners with basic computer and web-application literacy. No prior programming or Python experience is required; we focus on visual agent builders, low-code n8n AI Agent nodes, JSON tool schemas, and supervised prototyping. Optional code-first concepts are demonstrated, but visual mastery is the primary evaluated pathway.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer: The course spans 6 Weeks (48 total instructional hours, at 8 hours per week: 4 hours of live technical instruction and 4 hours of supervised studio lab). The transparent institutional fee is exactly ₹7,900,. The final payable amount, including any applicable taxes, will be clearly displayed before payment. adhering to Truth in Pricing with zero artificial countdown markups or fake retail strike-throughs. Flexible two-installment options are available.

faq.question: What is the difference between a chatbot and an AI agent?
faq.answer: A traditional chatbot primarily communicates conversationally with a user, generating text based on pre-training and immediate prompt context. An AI agent uses a language model as a reasoning and decision engine to decompose user goals, select from permitted tools (such as database searches or API calls), observe tool results, and complete multi-step tasks within bounded operational guardrails.

faq.question: What is the difference between AI agents and n8n automation?
faq.answer: Deterministic automations (like standard n8n workflows) follow predefined, hardcoded conditional paths (e.g. 'If email contains X, do Y'). An AI agent operates with bounded autonomy: the model evaluates incoming input dynamically and decides which tools to call, in what sequence, and with what arguments to achieve the user's objective, while respecting safety constraints.

faq.question: Will I learn how AI agents use tools?
faq.answer: Yes. Tool calling is a central pillar of the curriculum (Module 03). You will learn how models inspect tool names, descriptions, and JSON parameter schemas, select appropriate tools for specific sub-tasks, receive and interpret tool execution results, and handle tool errors or timeouts.

faq.question: What is function calling?
faq.answer: Function calling (or tool calling) is a model capability where an LLM detects when external tools are needed, pauses generation, and outputs structured JSON containing the function name and validated arguments. The host application executes the tool locally and returns the result to the model, ensuring external code execution remains under developer control.

faq.question: Will I learn MCP fundamentals?
faq.answer: Yes. We introduce the core architectural concepts of the Model Context Protocol (MCP): why the open standard exists, client/server relationships, tools vs resources vs prompts, tool discovery mechanisms, trust boundaries, and user permission models. Complex custom MCP server engineering is reserved for advanced tracks.

faq.question: Do I need Python programming?
faq.answer: No. Advanced Python programming is not mandatory. You will learn to construct, configure, and inspect agents using supported visual agent builders, OpenAI agent tooling, and n8n's visual AI Agent nodes. Basic understanding of JSON syntax and API concepts is taught step-by-step during the course.

faq.question: Will I build actual agent prototypes?
faq.answer: Yes. You will build, test, and document two complete, supervised agent prototypes: (1) a Tool-Using Business Information Assistant that answers inquiries with verified source attribution, and (2) a Safe Business Task-Routing Agent that chooses allowed tools and pauses for human approval before sensitive actions.

faq.question: How many practical projects are included?
faq.answer: The portfolio consists of three concrete deliverables: (1) The Tool-Using Business Information Assistant, (2) The Safe Business Task-Routing Agent, and (3) The 15-Case Agent Evaluation & Safety Test Suite with full trace logs and 5-dimension rubric scores.

faq.question: What is human-in-the-loop approval?
faq.answer: Human-in-the-loop (HITL) approval is a critical safety architecture where sensitive or consequential agent actions (such as sending customer emails, modifying database records, or initiating financial transactions) are paused before execution. The agent creates a staged action proposal, alerts a human reviewer, and only executes if valid approval is granted.

faq.question: Will I learn prompt-injection awareness?
faq.answer: Yes, prompt-injection defense is a compulsory topic (Module 05). You will learn the difference between direct user prompt overrides and indirect prompt injections concealed within retrieved documents or third-party tool responses, and how to implement pre-execution permission checks and output sanitization.

faq.question: What are AI agent guardrails?
faq.answer: Guardrails are layered programmatic safeguards that restrict agent behavior. They include input validation filters, role and instruction boundary constraints, tool-level permission checks (principle of least privilege), human approval checkpoints, and output schema validators. Guardrails significantly reduce risk but do not guarantee complete immunity.

faq.question: Does the course include agent testing?
faq.answer: Yes. Thorough empirical testing is a core learning outcome. You will learn how to create test datasets, assess agents against normal requests, evaluate ambiguous inputs, test tool selection traps, verify permission denials, and document failure recovery.

faq.question: What is included in the 15-case evaluation dataset?
faq.answer: The 15-case evaluation dataset includes: 5 valid requests with expected responses, 3 incorrect or ambiguous tool-selection traps, 2 permission error and human approval tests, 3 prompt-injection attacks (direct, indirect in document, and inside tool responses), and 2 failure recovery tests (tool timeout and malformed response).

faq.question: Will I learn agent tracing and debugging?
faq.answer: Yes. You will learn how to inspect observable execution traces—including incoming user prompts, selected tools, generated arguments, tool execution output, and decision timestamps. We emphasize observable operational debugging rather than speculating on unobservable internal model chain-of-thought.

faq.question: Does the course teach advanced multi-agent systems?
faq.answer: No. This course focuses on single-agent architecture, bounded autonomy, tool calling, and safety. Complex multi-agent orchestration frameworks (such as CrewAI, AutoGen, and LangGraph multi-agent swarms) are advanced engineering topics covered in Nova Skills' longer AI Solutions Engineering programme.

faq.question: Are paid AI API subscriptions compulsory?
faq.answer: No. You are not required to maintain multiple expensive enterprise subscriptions. We utilize budget-controlled test accounts, sandbox endpoints, and visual builder environments with minimal token usage. We also teach you how to forecast execution costs and manage API token budgets responsibly.

faq.question: Does this course include production agent deployment?
faq.answer: No. The course focuses on designing, prototyping, testing, and evaluating safe agent architectures in controlled studio environments. Enterprise Kubernetes clustering, high-availability server deployment, and production DevOps infrastructure are outside the scope of this foundational certification.

This verifies your practical competency and portfolio deliverables; it is not an official vendor certification issued by OpenAI, Anthropic, or n8n.
